taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes the Brazilian Dove (L. brasiliensis) is included in this species but regarded by some as a separate species (AOU 1983).
fieldMarks: 25-30 cm, round-bodied and short-tailed with pale eyes
Lacks the black ear spot and black wing spots of Mourning Dove
Rich dark chestnut under the wings in flight
behavior: Forages mostly on the ground, walking in woodland undergrowth; sometimes in low trees or shrubs
Usually solitary, not sociable like many doves; a few may gather at food sources
Eats seeds (grasses, mesquite, elm), berries and fruits such as hackberry and prickly pear, and possibly some insects
Song is a deep, drawn-out, descending coo lower pitched than most of our pigeons and doves
habitat: Shady woodlands and river thickets; in southern Texas any dense low growth, most common in native woodland but also second growth. Elsewhere in its range mostly drier or more open woods; avoids unbroken rain forest.
range: Permanent resident from northern Mexico and southern Texas (lower Rio Grande Valley) south to southern Brazil, Uruguay and eastern Argentina.

lookalikes.name: Mourning dove
lookalikes.howToTell: White-tipped is much rounder-bodied and shorter-tailed with pale eyes, and lacks the black ear spot and black wing spots.
